observations.observation: Before the revised figure circulated, Axios reported OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate near $70bn, with more than 70% growth since the start of Q3. The report attributed the number to unnamed people familiar with the financials.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This was a media report, not formal or audited company guidance; Axios said it had not obtained expense details.

observations.observation: By the Bloomberg search result's displayed 11:04 AM CST time on Oct. 8, coverage put OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50bn and below recent estimates, with the headline crediting the FT. This shows the report was circulating before cutoff, but does not verify the FT article's exact first-publication time or calculation basis.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The Bloomberg article body was inaccessible and the FT pre-cutoff version was not verified. The reports describe annualized run rate, not a confirmed $20bn reduction in recognized revenue.

observations.observation: Barron’s contemporaneous item reported broad-index declines after the FT story: Nasdaq Composite −1.4%, S&P 500 −0.7%, and Dow −0.1% (56 points).
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is an index-level report with temporal attribution, not causal isolation; the supplied passage does not identify Intel orders, customers, or production changes.

gaps: The FT article's exact first-publication time and its wording in a pre-cutoff snapshot remain unverified; its retrieved version shows an update time of 20:15 on Oct. 8 with no timezone.
No direct OpenAI disclosure or underlying investor financial presentation was verified in the eligible material.

The eligible pre-cutoff material does not resolve whether the near-$50bn and near-$70bn run-rate figures use the same definition or accounting treatment; do not characterize the difference as an actual revenue contraction or formal guidance miss.
No verified pre-cutoff source in this collection isolates other same-session market drivers or links the OpenAI report to an Intel-specific customer, order, deployment, or supply change.
